title: SLUS-20565
knowledge: Convention: to force a required sequence of stores to a struct in pure C (inline asm is not allowed), declare the affected fields volatile and write the assignments in the desired order. Verified byte-identical on func_00113460.

Wrapper that calls one function with a frame (jal + ld $ra) instead of tail-calling with `j`: give the wrapper return type s64 while the callee returns s32, e.g. `s64 f(s32 a){ return g(a, 6); }`. The return-mode mismatch stops the sibcall and adds no instructions. Verified byte-identical on func_002DA558.

Indirect call through a function-pointer table (lui $v0,%hi(tbl+off); lw $v0,%lo(tbl+off)($v0); jalr $v0): a direct `(*(void(**)())(tbl+off))()` gives $v1 for the lui. Write it as `u8 *p = tbl; p = *(u8 **)(p + off); ((void (*)(void *))p)(arg0);` to get $v0 throughout. Verified byte-identical on func_0015DE74, func_00165AB4, func_00165990.

A callee's return type matters even when the result is ignored: if a scratch value right after a call lands in $v1 where yours lands in $v0, declare that callee as returning a value (e.g. func_003021B0 is memset: `void *func_003021B0(void *, s32, s32)`). The call then sets $v0 and the allocator avoids it. Verified byte-identical on func_00154828 (two such spots, after func_003021B0 and func_0016AE78; s32 return for the latter).

Varargs functions (a1..a7 stored with sd into the top of the frame and the address of the first slot passed on as a va_list): system includes aren't allowed, so write va_start yourself as the EABI macro does: `char *ap = (char *)__builtin_next_arg(fmt) - (8 - __builtin_args_info(0)) * 8;` then pass ap. Verified byte-identical on func_002D70D0 (with try_compiler).

12-byte unaligned struct copy (ldl/ldr + lw + sdl/sdr + sw, then pass &copy to a callee): use `typedef struct __attribute__((packed, aligned(4))) { u64 a; s32 b; } P12; P12 copy = *p;` (non-volatile). Verified byte-identical on func_002BE0C8, func_002BBC90. Packed with only u8 b[12] gives lwl/lwr for the tail (wrong). Also: sh/swc1 init functions match with an all-volatile struct, float constants as locals loaded first, stores in target order (func_002BE1E8, func_002BBC48, func_002BA630).

Vtable-style indirect call (lw $v0,0x4C($a0); lw $v0,off($v0); jalr $v0). Use a `void *` temporary that you reassign, not `u8 *`: `void *p = *(void **)((u8 *)obj + 0x4C); p = *(void **)((u8 *)p + off); ((void (*)(void *, ...))p)(obj, ...);`. With `u8 *p`, or a direct expression, the call can land in $v1 (score 10-15). Verified byte-identical on func_0014B870 (5 args, which had failed 17 times), func_0014CECC, func_0014CF0C, func_0014CF78 and func_0014CE60.

g++ 2.9x virtual calls (lw vt,0x60(obj); addiu e,vt,N*8; lh delta,0(e); lw fn,4(e); jalr fn; addu a0,obj,delta): model the vtable entry as `typedef struct { s16 delta; s16 index; s32 (*fn)(void *, ...); } VEnt;` and call `VEnt *e = &obj->vt[N]; e->fn((char *)obj + e->delta, ...);`. Declare fn as RETURNING s32 even if the result is unused: with a void fn the entry pointer and fn swap $v0/$v1 (score 25); with s32 it matches. Verified byte-identical on func_002B6C68.

Handwritten asm stub, unmatchable in pure C. Assembly is `addiu $3,$0,0x23; syscall 0` with no `jr $ra` (noreturn). Per ps2sdk syscallnr.h, 0x23 = ExitThread, 0x3C = SetupThread (RFU060), 0x3D = SetupHeap (RFU061). _start passes this function's address in $8 to syscall 0x3C (SetupThread(gp,stack,stacksize,args,rootfunc)), so this is the main-thread root func = ExitThread stub from crt0.s. Tried __asm__ volatile li+syscall with noreturn attribute; rejected: `inline assembly is not allowed: matches must come from C`. No pure-C construct in ee-gcc 2.96 emits `syscall`. Suggest keeping crt0/_start + this stub as .s assembly and rename_symbol 0x00100250 -> ExitThread (or _exit_thread / LoopThread root). Do not spend C compiles here.

Semantics (fully understood): returns a float scale.
  f = 1.0f; if (g == 2) f = 1.3f (D_0047FC74); else if (g < 3) { if (g == 0) f = 0.7f (D_0047FC70); } else if (h == 3) f = 5.0f;
  if (h == 2) f = f * 1.7f (D_0047FC78); return f;
  g = D_00484CD8, h = D_00484538 (0x47FC70 = 0.7f, 0x47FC74 = 1.3f, 0x47FC78 = 1.7f).
The C structure above is certainly right - the TEST ORDER the ROM wants is beq g,2 / slti g<3 / beqz g,0,
i.e. exactly 'if (g==2) ... else if (g<3) { if (g==0) ... } else if (h==3) ...'. Everything else that is left is
GCC's BLOCK ORDER and its branch-likely choices.

Target layout (33 insns): entry(0x00) -> beq g,2 -> 0x50 (body B) ; slti/beqz -> 0x30 (the g>=3 block, tests
h==3, jumps to 0x6c) ; beqz g -> 0x40 (body A) ; 0x40 and 0x50 both 'b 0x68' ; 0x60 = the 5.0f body FALLS
THROUGH into 0x68 (join) ; each of the 4 paths does its own 'lw h' in the jump delay slot and joins at
0x6c (the 'bne h,2' multiply test).
So block order is entry, default-block(g>=3), body A, body B, body C(5.0f), join - NOT source order.

Best attempt so far (score 1030, 68.7%): a switch(g){case 0:case 1:case 2: default:}. It produces the same
test sequence but GCC peels case 1 first (beq g,1 / slti g<2 / beqz g) instead of case 2, and puts the
blocks in a different order. Note: case order in the source makes no difference, GCC sorts the case list.
Tried and worse: if-chain with '!=2' first test (1520 - gets 'beq g,2 -> 0x50' exactly right but GCC then
uses beql and loses the g==0 test), plain if-chain (1690 - GCC inverts the first branch and puts the body
inline), if-chain with explicit dead else branches (1690/1790).
Things to try next: make the g==2 body a block GCC will not inline (e.g. the 1.3f load through a helper
expression), or find a source form where the 'else if (h==3)' body falls through to the join (the 5.0f
block at 0x60 falls into 0x68, every other body jumps).

The issue is that the compiler treats D_004538E0 as a $gp-relative small data symbol, but the original code uses absolute addressing via lui/addiu. Declaring the global with or without extern doesn't change this behavior. The function structure is correct; only the address computation differs.

  L348 (loop head, 2 preds): i = 0; if (*arg1 == 0) return p; if (*arg1 != p[i]) goto L980; i++; p++;
  L370 (inner loop): if (arg1[i] == 0) return p; if (arg1[i] != p[i]) goto L980; i++; p++; backedge
  L980 (latch): if (*p != 0) goto L348; else return NULL;
BLOCKER: gcc CSEs the entry's '*p' load with the loop head's 'p[i]' load (same address, no stores anywhere in the function), hoists it into the entry block's delay slot as an LBU, and then needs sll/sra + bne for the comparison. The ROM reloads 'lb $2,0($4)' inside L348 and compares the two raw lbu/lb values. Tried: entry test via *(volatile s8*)p (then the entry test itself became lbu/bnel and the loop rotated the other way), while-loop instead of do-while (rotates the other way and duplicates the movz), goto/next vs continue vs nested if. All end at 40-46 instructions vs 33.
NEXT IDEA for whoever picks it up: the ROM's two loads are NOT merged, so something in the original stops the CSE - maybe the entry test reads the parameter (arg0) while the loop reads a copy that gcc cannot equate (e.g. p assigned inside the loop body), or the strings are read through a union/typedef with a different char signedness on one side. Also the inner loop must not be peeled a second time: only the i=0 iteration is peeled in the ROM.

GCC's BLOCK ORDER and its branch-likely choices.

Target layout (33 insns): entry(0x00) -> beq g,2 -> 0x50 (body B) ; slti/beqz -> 0x30 (the g>=3 block, tests
h==3, jumps to 0x6c) ; beqz g -> 0x40 (body A) ; 0x40 and 0x50 both 'b 0x68' ; 0x60 = the 5.0f body FALLS
THROUGH into 0x68 (join) ; each of the 4 paths does its own 'lw h' in the jump delay slot and joins at
0x6c (the 'bne h,2' multiply test).
So block order is entry, default-block(g>=3), body A, body B, body C(5.0f), join - NOT source order.

The C structure above is certainly right - the TEST ORDER the ROM wants is beq g,2 / slti g<3 / beqz g,0,
i.e. exactly 'if (g==2) ... else if (g<3) { if (g==0) ... } else if (h==3) ...'. Everything else that is left is
GCC's BLOCK ORDER and its branch-likely choices.

Target layout (33 insns): entry(0x00) -> beq g,2 -> 0x50 (body B) ; slti/beqz -> 0x30 (the g>=3 block, tests
h==3, jumps to 0x6c) ; beqz g -> 0x40 (body A) ; 0x40 and 0x50 both 'b 0x68' ; 0x60 = the 5.0f body FALLS
THROUGH into 0x68 (join) ; each of the 4 paths does its own 'lw h' in the jump delay slot and joins at
0x6c (the 'bne h,2' multiply test).
So block order is entry, default-block(g>=3), body A, body B, body C(5.0f), join - NOT source order.

MATCHED 2026-10-22. Key tricks for ee-gcc 2.96:
- Local temp structs a (sp+0x10) and b (sp+0x40) are accessed through a scoped pointer (`Vec3 *ap = &a;`) so the a.x store is not forwarded and reloads from memory, exactly like target; the pointer is callee-saved and reused ($s2) across both blocks.
- Keep a.x / a.y in f32 locals across the second call: `f32 ax = call1 * -5.0f; f32 ay = call2 * -5.0f; ap->x = ax; ap->z = 30.0f; ap->y = ay;` -> f20 holds ax (in delay slot of second jal), 30.0f in f22.
- Vector updates must be written x,y,z order (`pos->x +=; pos->y +=; pos->z +=;`) so the target load order x(f3),y(f2),z(f1) appears; scheduler then emits stores z,y,x.
- Pass the by-value struct with assignment inside the args: `func_001815C8(draw = *pos, ...)`. Args are evaluated right-to-left, so the last arg (func_0015A100(...)*1000 + D_00481548) is computed BEFORE the *pos copy; a separate `draw = *pos;` statement forces the copy first and shifts regalloc.
- `volatile Vec3 pad;` is needed to force the 0x90 frame. Layout: saved sp+0, a sp+0x10, pad sp+0x20, draw sp+0x30, b sp+0x40.
- func_001815C8 is EABI: Vec3 by value passed as hidden pointer in a0 (copy at sp+0x30), then a1=0xFA,a2=0x96,a3=0,t0=0x28,t1=D_00484F70,t2=0,t3=2,f12=5.0f,f13=last arg.
- s32 D_004844A4 (<<14), s32 D_00484F70, f32 D_00481548 are gp-relative; declare as non-extern.

So block order is entry, default-block(g>=3), body A, body B, body C(5.0f), join - NOT source order.

The C structure above is certainly right - the TEST ORDER the ROM wants is beq g,2 / slti g<3 / beqz g,0,
i.e. exactly 'if (g==2) ... else if (g<3) { if (g==0) ... } else if (h==3) ...'. Everything else that is left is
GCC's BLOCK ORDER and its branch-likely choices.

Target layout (33 insns): entry(0x00) -> beq g,2 -> 0x50 (body B) ; slti/beqz -> 0x30 (the g>=3 block, tests
h==3, jumps to 0x6c) ; beqz g -> 0x40 (body A) ; 0x40 and 0x50 both 'b 0x68' ; 0x60 = the 5.0f body FALLS
THROUGH into 0x68 (join) ; each of the 4 paths does its own 'lw h' in the jump delay slot and joins at
0x6c (the 'bne h,2' multiply test).
So block order is entry, default-block(g>=3), body A, body B, body C(5.0f), join - NOT source order.
